summary:
AstroCare 360 is an adaptive, offline-first health monitoring and emergency triage platform designed for deep-space crews and remote clinics on Earth.

The platform consists of two integrated components connected via a cloud database:

The Astronaut App: Empowers non-doctor crew members to autonomously perform medical triage using an interactive 3D body explorer, follow step-by-step first aid and emergency treatment protocols, monitor vital signs against spaceflight hazards(such as SANS and cosmic radiation), and maintain mental health through an asynchronous family messaging hub and stress-relief suite. It automatically adapts its diagnostic thresholds whether the crew is in orbital transit, on a lunar base, or facing radiation storms.
The Medical Centre Portal: Gives ground-based flight surgeons a organized dashboard to track astronaut health trends, view prioritized triage requests, and send asynchronous clinical guidance across communication delays.

Why It Matters: On missions far from Earth with limited supplies and communication latency, early autonomous medical evaluation prevents minor health issues from becoming life-threatening emergencies. Furthermore, AstroCare 360 translates directly to Earth as an offline telemedicine tool for rural, underserved, and disaster-relief communities where professional physicians are unavailable.
details:
1. What does it do or how does it work?

AstroCare 360 is a two-part web platform designed for deep-space crew health autonomy and ground mission medical support.

  • The Astronaut App: Empowers non-doctor crew members to autonomously perform medical triage using an interactive 3D human body explorer. Selecting affected body regions triggers plain-language diagnostic steps, vital checks, and first-aid protocols[1]. The app tracks core vitals—such as blood pressure, heart rate, sleep quality, and Spaceflight Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS) indicators—alongside cumulative cosmic neutron radiation exposure.
  • Adaptive Environment Engine: Automatically switches diagnostic thresholds and risk alerts based on operational context: Deep Space Transit Mode (zero-g fluid shifts & muscle loss), Lunar/Mars Surface Base Mode (partial gravity, surface dust, and EVA fatigue), High Radiation Warning Mode (active solar flares and neutron spikes), and Earth Rural Telemedicine Mode.
  • "Heart & Crew Connection" Suite: Addresses behavioral health hazards through an asynchronous family messaging hub (built specifically to handle space-to-Earth communication latency), guided circadian sleep protocols, and crew stress-relief routines.
  • The Medical Centre Portal: Provides flight surgeons on Earth with an organized dashboard to monitor crew vital trends, view prioritized triage requests, and queue clinical advice. Both applications sync continuously via a unified cloud database whenever data links are available.

2. What benefits does it have?

  • Autonomous Deep-Space Survival: Allows crew members to evaluate emergencies and act immediately without waiting for ground support during interplanetary communication delays.
  • Preventative Healthcare: Helps identify minor physiological or psychological changes early, preventing them from escalating into life-threatening crises far from hospitals.
  • Comprehensive Well-Being: Protects both physical health (SANS, radiation damage, musculoskeletal atrophy) and mental health (isolation strain, sleep deprivation, crew tension).
  • Dual-Use Terrestrial Application: Functions offline-first as a remote telemedicine tool, allowing healthcare workers in isolated, rural, Antarctic, or disaster-relief communities on Earth to conduct structured patient assessments without a doctor present.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

  • Space Mission Impact: Protects astronaut safety and operational independence on long-duration Artemis lunar missions, surface bases, and crewed Mars expeditions.
  • Global Earth Impact: Promotes global health equity by adapting deep-space emergency technology into accessible, offline healthcare solutions for underserved populations on Earth.
  • Challenge Alignment: Positioned for the Galactic Impact (most potential to improve life on Earth or in space) and Best Mission Concept award categories.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did we use?

  • Front-End Framework & UI: React, Tailwind CSS, Lucide Icons, Framer Motion, and Three.js / WebGL (for the interactive 3D human body model).
  • UI/UX Prototyping: Lovable (for component design and layout orchestration).
  • AI Clinical Engine: Google AI Studio / Gemini 1.5 Pro API (configured with custom system instructions to parse clinical inputs and return structured JSON triage guidance, risk levels, and treatment protocols).
  • Database & Cloud Sync: Supabase / REST backend (for cross-platform message queuing, asynchronous media storage, and state synchronization).

5. How is our project creative?

  • Unified Physical & Mental Hub: Combines emergency clinical triage with psychological connection tools in a single user interface.
  • Visual 3D Selection: Replaces dense medical text manuals with an intuitive, interactive 3D body explorer that non-physicians can operate under high stress.
  • Location-Aware Logic: Dynamically adapts baseline physiological thresholds depending on whether the crew is orbiting, walking on the Moon/Mars, or experiencing a solar storm.
  • Latency-Native Communication: Accepts interplanetary communication delays as a design constraint, offering asynchronous video/voice note queues rather than unrealistic live calling.

6. What factors did our team consider?

  • NASA HRP's 5 Spaceflight Hazards: Space radiation, isolation & confinement, distance from Earth, gravity fields, and hostile/closed environments.
  • Communication Latency: Light-speed delays ranging from minutes to hours between Earth and deep space, requiring onboard autonomy.
  • Non-Doctor Usability: Designing touch targets and simplified step-by-step guidance so non-physician crew members can execute procedures during emergencies.
  • Global Dual-Use: Ensuring that every feature built for deep-space hazards offers tangible, offline health benefits for remote communities on Earth.
